title: Migrant Caravans Cannot Cross Into the US and Are Told So, Sheinbaum Clarifies to Trump
author: SinEmbargo Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo Editorial
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[November 12, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4902660/las-caravanas-de-migrantes-no-
pueden-cruzar-a-eu-y-se-les-informa-aclara-csp-a-trump/), a Mexican digital
news outlet._

_The president emphasized the National Migration Institute’s experience in
assisting these caravans and persuading people to return to their countries or
remain in Mexico under certain conditions._

**Mexico City, November 12 (SinEmbargo).-** [**President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/claudia-sheinbaum/) clarified to her
counterpart **Donald Trump** that no **migrant caravan** has reached the
northern border since he arrived at the White House, after the U.S. president
threatened to double tariffs on Mexico if these groups of people approached
the border.

> “Since President Trump took office, no migrant caravan has reached the
> northern border. There are two caravans at the moment, one in Arriaga,
> Chiapas, which had formed with around 500-600 people, and now fewer than 100
> people remain. How do we do this? We inform the people in the caravan that
> it is very difficult to cross into the United States (US), that if their
> goal is to cross into the US, they will not be able to do so, because that
> possibility does not exist. We seek to have them return safely to their
> country, or if someone wants to stay in Mexico, under certain conditions, in
> a particular place, they can do so. But the vast majority return to their
> countries of origin. Once they learn they will not be able to cross the
> Mexican border with the US,” she said.

Sheinbaum rejected the use of repression against the caravans. She described
the National Guard and migration authorities as accompanying people and
explaining their options. She linked the recent increase in caravans to false
claims that the US midterm election results had eased immigration rules, which
she said remained unchanged. Migrants were being offered assistance to return
home voluntarily or, under certain conditions, stay in Mexico.

Trump threatened an immediate doubling of tariffs on Mexican exports unless
Mexico stopped the groups. His warning named Mexican authorities, US Border
Patrol, ICE and the governor of Texas.
